::: {#sol-clipped}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
clipped_rnn = make_reader(nn.RNN, 1)
_ = train(clipped_rnn, n_epochs=20, max_norm=1)
clipped_acc = accuracy(clipped_rnn)
print(clipped_acc)
# The prose below says the reader is still below the row reader.
assert clipped_acc < row_acc
```

With [gradient clipping](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-gradient-clipping),
the pixel reader classifies `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$clipped_acc)` of the test digits correctly,
against `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$pixel_acc)` without it.
`r if (py$clipped_acc > py$pixel_acc) "So clipping helps" else "So clipping does not help"`.
Clipping caps the size of each [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient),
so no gradient [Adam](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-adam) sees can be as large as the spikes of @fig-grad-norms.
The reader is still `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (py$row_acc - py$clipped_acc))` percentage points below the row reader of @sol-rows.

:::
